### Worked rule: CC → RTU

On **Firewall Rules**, open **Create rule** below the table. Set ID
`control-centre-to-rtu-iec104`, action ALLOW, source zone `lan4`, destination
zone `lan1`, source `10.60.60.20/32`, destination `10.30.30.20/32`, protocol
TCP and port 2404. Stage the rule. Use **Move to… → top** so the required
exception precedes the broader deny. Saving and moving only stage edits.

Equivalent commands from the fw-1 configuration CLI (create once, not both
UI and CLI; if the ID exists, edit it with `set` instead of adding it again):

    add firewall rule control-centre-to-rtu-iec104 ALLOW lan4 lan1
    set firewall rule control-centre-to-rtu-iec104 --sources 10.60.60.20/32 --destinations 10.30.30.20/32 --protocols tcp:2404
    move firewall rule control-centre-to-rtu-iec104 top

Repeat this create → pin → order procedure for the other five conduits.
Create the four logged diagnostic DENY rules below; Weak has none. Use
`log: true` (the form's Log setting, or `set firewall rule <id> --log true`).
Each rule accepts source zones wan, dmz, lan1, lan2, lan3, lan4, lan5 and
TCP only; destination scope is below. Do not add a management allow or
change the reserved management envelope.

| Rule ID | Destination zone / address | TCP port | Place after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deny-unauthorized-iec104` | lan1, any station address | 2404 | CC→RTU allow |
| `deny-unauthorized-modbus` | lan2, any field address | 502 | RTU and PLC allows |
| `deny-unauthorized-historian-ingest` | lan5, 10.70.70.40/32 | 8081 | CC ingest allow |
| `deny-unauthorized-plc-web` | lan1, 10.30.30.30/32 | 8080 | engineering web allow |

Under a partial request, keep deferred allows before overlapping denies.
The first matching enforcing rule wins. Review the full candidate; never
commit the temporary broad rule created by `add` before applying its pins.

Before the single commit, compare the complete candidate with your request.
On **Configuration**, **Review changes** leads with entity summaries;
**Advanced** opens the exact JSON diff. Have a second reviewer check deletes,
replacements and surviving rules, not just the edited row.

From the fw-1 configuration CLI, commit replacements and removals together:

    show diff
    commit confirmed 60

Or use **Commit-confirmed** on **Configuration** after review and set the
seconds field to the agreed test window. `60` is an example: agree enough
time for management and operational checks before starting. Make ONE commit
for this rule change. Read back with `show running-config`; record the
running identity, UTC time and confirmation deadline. Check management access
through the portal and the required operational conduits before confirming.
From the fw-1 configuration CLI, retain the change only after those checks pass:

    confirm

Or use **Confirm** while the deadline is pending. Without `confirm`, containd
restores the previous running config at the deadline. If a rollback trigger
occurs, stop testing, notify the operator and do not confirm. The rollback
owner checks the restored running identity and retests operations. For an
immediate return, use `rollback` (UI **Recovery → Rollback**). Rollback is one
level only: it restores the previous running config, not an arbitrary history.
The UI rollback keeps the newer staged candidate; do not commit it accidentally.
Reserved management protection refuses unsafe changes and rollback targets.

Reconnect CC and check all six operational conduits before confirming.
Retest from the named sources in Phases 5 and 6. Keep the pre-change export
as a restorable backup and evidence reference.

:::hint No semantic enforcement claim
Create the six L4 allows and four diagnostic denies before adding monitoring. If the request
includes **Monitor IEC 104 commands**, add `observe-cc-breaker-command`,
`observe-cc-oltc-step` and `observe-cc-oltc-raise-only` as separate IEC 104
rules, each explicitly `mode: monitor`. Never overlay a monitor predicate
on an operational allow. Monitor ALLOW does not admit traffic and monitor
DENY does not deny it. The L4 source pin enforces; DPI detects and logs.
Monitoring never satisfies a BLOCK requirement; Modbus DPI remains planning-only.
:::

### Do this
- Check a post-commit CC connection, completed GI and valid current inventory.
- With operator approval, perform the controlled OLTC regulation demonstration below.
- Verify RTU field telemetry, PLC motion and historian ingest independently.
- Run historian and PLC-web reads from **Kali** and **eng-ws** respectively.
- Record all six conduit results, plant health, policy identity and UTC times in Notes.

Prove all six required operational intents, not merely open sockets. In the Control Centre require a completed current-connection general interrogation (GI) and every inventory point non-null and valid, received at or after that attempt’s GI start. Quiet status does not need advancing receipt times; float quality includes the reporting watchdog. Include F2 position, protection trip, lockout, current and MW (indication only, no command). Confirm RTU field telemetry and a healthy PLC heartbeat; observe an actual PLC request and its motion after the policy change. Check CC historian ingest and advancing archive samples separately from reader access.

:::hint Use your live operator connection
Reconnect CC after the commit using the Phase 4 procedure. Check that
`link.since` is later than the commit, then wait for the connect GI to finish.
Interrogate station on an old connection does not test a new handshake.
Keep the GI start/completion and current-connection identity with your results.
If GI evidence is missing or more than ten minutes old, press **Interrogate
station** before collecting PLC and historian observations. Routine GI runs
on connect and every 15 minutes. Quiet status does not need new receipt times.
:::

:::hint Monitoring semantics and forwarding dependency
The L4 source pin enforces; DPI detects and logs. Monitoring never satisfies
a BLOCK requirement. Select-before-operate (**SBO**) sequences a command;
it is not authorization. A double command (**C_DC**) addresses an information
object address (**IOA**); observing it does not prevent its operation.

**Forwarding dependency:** monitor traffic traverses NFQUEUE 101 and adds engine processing latency. There is no queue bypass; if the engine is down, the CC conduit drops. Monitor-only does not mean availability-neutral. Preserve rollback and prove GI, PLC and historian continuity independently; do not deliberately stop the engine for this lesson.
:::

:::hint Optional depth: shadow counters and approved breaker operations

For Hardened, or a plan selecting **Monitor IEC 104 commands**, inspect the embedded containd **Firewall/ICS tables** and running configuration. Confirm DPI and the IEC 104 decoder are healthy, NFQUEUE is **101**, and all three separate rules are applied with `protocol: iec104`, explicit `mode: monitor`, `direction: request`, CA **1**, and CC **10.60.60.20** → RTU **10.30.30.20 TCP/2404** (lan4→lan1):
Expand **Inspect rule** for Conditions, ICS Filter and full Shadow matches. On ICS, inspect **Active inspection**, **Why?** and **Inspection details**; **Technical details** retains queue/interface values.

| Rule ID | Configured action | Selectors |
|---|---|---|
| `observe-cc-breaker-command` | DENY (monitor) | Double command (C_DC), Type 46, information object address (IOA) 3001 |
| `observe-cc-oltc-step` | ALLOW (monitor) | Type 47, IOA 3301, COT 6, states [1,2], QU [0], negative false, test false |
| `observe-cc-oltc-raise-only` | ALLOW (monitor) | Same OLTC selectors, but states [2] |

**Reconnect CC first** with the Phase 4 procedure: inspection starts only at a fresh SYN, not halfway through the old session. Wait for connect GI, then record a shadow-counter baseline from the embedded tables: `available: true`, all three rule IDs, `snapshotVersion`, `since`, `unit` and each rule's `shadowMatches`, `wouldAllow`, `wouldDeny`. Counters reset on every successful apply and are lost on engine restart. `available:false` is never zero; a missing applied rule is not zero either. If the snapshot or since changes, discard the comparison and establish a new baseline after reconnect/GI. A plan deferring **Monitor IEC 104 commands** has no such rules: record observation work as deferred, not as zero matches or prevention.

Correlate a prescribed, approved CC breaker operation with `observe-cc-breaker-command` `wouldDeny` increasing by **≥1**, `ics.decision` (`mode: monitor`, `decision: would_drop`, `reason: rule`, matching `ruleId` and UTC window), fresh feedback and the actual field result. Restore normal breaker/supply state before continuing. The monitor DENY does not stop CB1 operating; it is a rule-local hypothetical decision, not a denied command or a whole-policy prediction. See [monitor evidence](/knowledge#eu-ics-dpi).

:::

**Operator-authorized operational demonstration — controlled regulation loop.** First wait for a settled tap and the 20.196–20.604 kV band (20.4 kV ±1%). Reset starts at zero but the profile-disabled nominal equilibrium is +2, about 20.429 kV; the daily profile normally keeps running. When regulation is quiescent the PLC sends no tap request, so perturb regulation and let automatic control correct it, producing a PLC-originated request to observe. These control writes are not
acceptance reads. Obtain operator approval first; do not copy them into the
read-only acceptance tests in Lab 2.4. Use the **Control Centre** selected-device faceplate or the [operator API](/knowledge#eu-rtu-control-centre-apis); read tap, auto and voltage from `GET /api/operator/state` and wait for completed feedback before each command — an in-flight step returns 409:

1. Select **manual**: command `oltc-1-mode` → `manual`. Verify the auto feedback (IOA 1303) clears before continuing.
2. Request `oltc-1-step` → `lower`, wait for completed feedback, then one
   `raise` and wait again to restore that tap. This verifies adjacent motion;
   it is not yet proof of PLC automatic correction.
3. Now request **two lower steps**, waiting for completed feedback after each, to exercise automatic correction next. Watch IOA 1301 go transient, then settle at each adjacent tap. One step can remain inside the band and would not prove automatic correction. See [step telemetry](/knowledge#eu-iec104-step-telemetry).
4. Return to **auto**: `oltc-1-mode` → `auto`. Wait for the configured 30 s sustained demand, then the 2 s motion for each correction; IOA 2403 reports configured delay, not its countdown. Automatic control now issues PLC-originated Modbus requests toward the operating band, not necessarily the exact starting tap under the daily profile. Confirm that PLC request, its motion completion and the solved revision, and that the historian ingests the advancing tap.

:::hint Optional depth: compare OLTC monitor matches
With **Monitor IEC 104 commands** applied, compare OLTC shadow evidence while manual: record counters, request `oltc-1-step` → `lower`, and wait for completed feedback. `observe-cc-oltc-step` must gain **≥1** match; `observe-cc-oltc-raise-only` must gain **0**. Then request one `raise` to restore that tap and wait: **both** rules must gain **≥1** match. Keep snapshotVersion/since unchanged and correlate rule/mode/time events with the field feedback. A successful fully decoded SBO action normally produces **2 matches** per matching rule (select + execute, both COT 6), but this is **not guaranteed**; early refusal can end the sequence. Count matching decoded messages, not successful operations. Never require exactly two or interpret missing/unavailable evidence as a non-match. If monitoring is deferred, still perform the lower/raise and check field feedback, but record shadow evidence as deferred.
:::

From the **Kali terminal**, read the historian:

    curl -fsS --max-time 3 http://10.70.70.40:8080/api/points

From the **eng-ws terminal**, retrieve the PLC login page:

    curl -fsS --max-time 3 http://10.30.30.30:8080/login

:::hint Continuity is a hard constraint
Both breakers closed, RMU1 closed/RMU2 open and a fresh (≤3 s) bus20/S1/S2/S3 supply solve are independently checked from field/process truth. OLTC remote/auto, PLC motion and fresh operator observations must survive. Record these operator observations alongside your source-specific tests. Same-subnet success is not firewall enforcement.
:::

:::hint Optional depth: instructor-supervised F2 visibility check
Save the policy and UTC window before temporarily over-restricting RTU→F2 Modbus. A commit re-evaluates established connections on their next packet against the current first-match policy. Traffic no longer admitted stops without session deletion. Sessions may retain the conntrack entry until timeout; its presence is not proof of delivery. Observe loss after commit and allow for protocol failure detection. F2's five last values must remain visible with INVALID / NOT TOPICAL and STALE (underlying reason `device_unreachable`) while other devices retain valid observations and the IEC 104 link stays started. This is observation loss, not proof that F2 opened. Restore the named F2 destination, request a new GI and retain all inventory points non-null and valid received since that GI start. Keep any loss, healthy-peer and recovery evidence locally with this optional exercise; Lab 2.4 does not require it. Do not issue an F2 supervisory command or reset its protection to repair communications.
:::

Record the six conduit results, device readings, operator name, UTC times and
running policy identity in Notes. Check fresh valid Control Centre points and
process continuity separately. Bridged rows are endpoint evidence, not proof
of a routed firewall rule. Stop and follow the agreed rollback if required
operations fail.
